title.narrative: Sesea Inc: Technical feasibility study for industrial Hemp/flax production in Sierra Leone

description.narrative: Industrial Hemp based fibres are highly sustainable and can be used for the production of textiles, furniture, construction materials, etc. They require 70% less water than regular cotton production, are (agro-)chemical free and intercrop friendly, they contribute to soil fertility, allow for a carbon efficient production system and are biodegradable. Furthermore, hemp based industries show positive results in poverty alleviation, create employment and provide high impact solutions for climate change issues and ecological restauration. Industrial Hemp is only limitedly cultivated on the African continent. In Sierra Leone in particular, agriculture is underdeveloped due to civil wars and the Ebola crisis. Many families heavily rely on the mining industries. Yet, Sierra Leone’s soil type, climate and length of dry season are very favourable for high yield hemp production.Sesea produces Hemp fibres for the growing eco-textile and bio-based raw material markets and aims to build a hemp based industry and supply chain and develop ‘cash crops’ in Africa to meet increasing international demand and help (re)build local economies. Therefore Sesea now wants to expand production to Sierra Leone. To prepare for future investments in an Industrial Hemp production facility, Technical Assistance (DGGF-TA) provided support to Sesea Inc to conduct a technical feasibility study into cultivation and production requirements. The project included a pilot cultivation field of 1 ha, 3 harvesting seasons and field tests with different seed varieties to determine optimal cultivation conditions and techniques, the production of a field guide based on research results and the development of a bankable business plan. Furthermore, fibres and wood chips were assessed for quality and usability for bio-based materials applications. The project has been successful and supported 5 direct jobs, 15 indirect jobs and provided sustainable knowledge transfer regarding the sustainable advantages of Industrial Hemp production to 30 people. Furthermore, the project has led to the opening of a local joint venture, the development of a bankable business plan and a guide for intercropping hemp production methods that will improve existing agricultural practices and benefit local communities. Further investments are currently being prepared and may result in a 20 ha production field and further product development which will require a minimum of 440 seasonal workers per season.
